consumer: NONE. This packet is written to the fixture path and handed to nobody.

trigger.detail: SECTOR-SF3 owner-approved TEST_FIXTURE execution (one attempt, no retry). A fixture unit has no sector state machine, so there is no Offer-Ready promotion and no Gate G - the authorisation IS the trigger, as in SECTOR-SF1 and SECTOR-SF2.

payload.verdict_label: SIMULATED_VERDICT: a mechanism fixture result, not a fit verdict. It says nothing about whether any real property fits.
payload.what_this_packet_carries: The computed fail-closed floors over all FOUR contributing elements, and nothing else. No finding, no angle, no audience, no offer match, no timing and no CRM tag - because fixture mode reads no live store.
payload.floor_inputs_source: The floors are derived from the RECORDED CONTRACT STATE in 01_Sector/contracts/sector-databases.json, which S10's header names as field truth and F0 permits as a repository file. NO live Notion store was read.

contributing_elements.three_state: PRESENT BUT NULL - not absent. The fields were added live 2026-10-02 by DB3-OD10-OD12-1 and every cell of both is null. Absent and present-but-null both fail closed; only the second can ever be filled.

confidence.detail: Medium on all 4 rows (non_null_detail, unchanged by the backfill)

next_review.detail: populated on Operator, Amplifier and Enabler (2026-11-24); NULL on Buyer - no review date is asserted anywhere for that row, and inheriting another row's date is explicitly forbidden

confidence.detail: 0 of 28 provenance cells populated, so Confidence is null on all 4 rows
0 of 399 provenance cells populated, so Confidence is null on all 57 rows

validation_rules.confidence_rule: ORDER Low < Medium < High. If ANY contributing item has a null Confidence -> UNRESOLVED, naming each such element; else the weakest value on ORDER. A null is UNASSESSED and weaker than Low.
validation_rules.freshness_rule: If ANY contributing item has a null Last Verified OR a null Next Review -> UNRESOLVED, naming each such element; else the EARLIEST Next Review as the rejection date with the OLDEST Last Verified.
validation_rules.no_substitution: No assembly date, current date, Freshness label or sibling row's date may substitute for either date. A borrowed date is a fabricated one.
validation_rules.three_state: A field may be absent, present-but-null, or present-and-populated. Absent and present-but-null both fail closed; only the second can be filled. Say which one is being reported.
validation_rules.boundary_law: An angle, never an artifact. This packet carries neither.

confidence_threshold.reason: DB 9 and DB 10 carry a NULL Confidence on every row (0 of 28 and 0 of 399 provenance cells), and a null is UNASSESSED - weaker than Low. The rule therefore returns UNRESOLVED naming each such element.
confidence_threshold.would_have_been: Medium, had DB 9 and DB 10 been assessed: DB 3 contributes Medium (214 of 217 rows Medium, 3 High) and DB 6 contributes Medium on all four rows. That per-element contribution is NOT the packet floor.
confidence_threshold.synthetic_cap: SYNTHETIC - the input is a constructed record and no attribute was observed, which caps everything in this packet regardless of the floor.
confidence_threshold.act_on: Nothing. This packet tests mechanism only.

freshness_requirement.rule: A consumer may reject on age. No rejection date can be stated, because no contributing element supplies both dates.

sla_cadence: None. A fixture has no SLA and creates no obligation.
failure_modes: Reading this packet as evidence about any real property, market, demand, buyer, capacity, price or performance. It is none of those.
Reading `simulated_verdict: in_scope` as a fit verdict. It is a mechanism result.
Reading the computed floors as a statement that the data is adequate. Both resolve to UNRESOLVED, which is the designed answer when provenance is absent.
Treating `not_attempted_fixture` as a delivery. Nothing was delivered anywhere.
Marking any PG gate passed. The PG ladder is defined over a real property; this run moves none of it.
